subject: Dedicated capacity vs Hyperscaler GPU eval — POC recap & next steps
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Smith <j.smith@acmeai.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity vs Hyperscaler GPU eval — recap + proposed next tests

Jordan — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so everyone is aligned.

Call recap (high level):
- You’re evaluating Redwood Dedicated vs hyperscaler managed GPUs for Acme’s customer-facing inference use case (high qps, low p95 latency, predictable spend).
- Key success criteria you called out: p95 latency under 150ms for 256-token responses, predictable token unit cost, regional data residency (US), and failover to second region.

Redwood differentiators we discussed:
- Dedicated/reserved capacity: GPU pools reserved for Acme with baseline throughput guarantees and a documented SLA (we can provide addendum).
- Production-first runtime: automatic batching, KV/prefix caching and optimized kernels to reduce unit cost while holding latency SLOs.
- Smart routing & fallback: policy-driven routing and automatic fallback to compatible variants when primary pool is constrained (minimize errors during spikes).
- Cost controls: per-route batching and quantization profiles; predictable billing for reserved pools.

Proposed validation tests (these are short, focused POC runs we recommend):
1) Sustained throughput test — 72h run at your expected steady-state qps (you mentioned ~200 concurrent requests, ~128 tokens avg). Measure p95/p99 latency and cost per 1k tokens.
2) Spike & recovery — 1h burst at 3x steady qps to validate burst capacity and rollback behavior.
3) Failover — simulate region outage and validate cross-region failover (<2 min recovery).
4) Cold-start/scale test — evaluate cold-latency for scaled-up nodes and prewarming benefits.

Next steps we propose:
- If Acme is comfortable, we’ll provision a small reserved pool (config below) for a two-week POC window and run test (1) and (2).
- We’ll share a POC plan and capacity profile (attached).
- Marissa (SE) will own technical setup and metrics collection; Laura will handle commercial/contract flow.

Suggested baseline reserved pool for the POC: 4 dedicated GPUs (80GB class) with prewarmed runtime and a small burst buffer to simulate production. We can adjust depending on your model and token profile.

Attachments: redwood_poc-plan.pdf (POC playbook) and redwood_capacity_profile.xlsx (recommended node counts + expected throughput).

Proposed kickoff window: Mar 10–12. Can you confirm availability and whether Procurement should be looped for the reserved capacity addendum?

Thanks — happy to sync live if easier.

— Markus Klein
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142

From: Jordan Smith <j.smith@acmeai.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmeai.com
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 11:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity vs Hyperscaler GPU eval — recap + proposed next tests

Thanks Markus — good summary. A few clarifying questions before we lock in dates: 

1) Can you confirm the formal capacity guarantee and SLA you’re willing to put in writing for reserved pools? We need uptime and latency commitments for the POC to validate operational fit.
2) How does burst capacity work? If we hit 3x qps for an hour, do we get additional headroom or throttling? What is the cost model for burst usage beyond the reserved baseline?
3) For the failover test: will failover be automatic or require manual failover triggers? How quickly does the system route traffic to the secondary region?
4) Pricing: can we get a ballpark for the POC reserved pool (monthly equivalent) so Procurement can pre-approve?

Looping in Procurement (procurement@acmeai.com) to start the commercial thread. Also adding Evan Lee from HyperscalerCloud — we’re comparing Redwood Dedicated to their reserved GPU offering; Evan, appreciate any documentation you can share on preemption behavior and billing for burst.

Best,
Jordan
Head of Platform — Acme AI
j.smith@acmeai.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity vs Hyperscaler GPU eval — recap + proposed next tests

Markus / Laura — quick internal note with technical clarifications we can feed back to Acme: 

SLA & guarantees:
- We offer a Dedicated Capacity addendum with a baseline throughput SLA (99.9% uptime for the reserved pool) and P95 latency SLOs for the configured profile. For POC we can commit to a testing SLA and provide detailed runbooks/incident contacts.

Burst behavior:
- Dedicated pools include a configurable burst buffer (short-term capacity that can be used when load spikes). Burst is not unlimited — typically sized to ~2–3x baseline for short durations (up to a few hours) and billed at a predefined rate. For the POC we can enable a conservative burst of 2.5x.

Failover:
- Cross-region failover is automatic when configured; typical routing propagation + warm standby handoff is ~90–180s depending on model size and KV cache warmup. We’ll capture exact timing during the failover test.

Suggested POC configuration (technical):
- 4 x 80GB-class GPUs (reserved), prewarmed containers, reserved KV cache shards for low cold-latency.
- Instrumentation: we’ll stream traces/metrics to the shared Grafana dashboard (p95, p99, cpu/gpu utilization, queue depth, token/sec, and cost metrics).
- Tests: 72h sustained run at 200 concurrent requests (~128 tokens avg), 1h 3x spike, cross-region failover simulation.

Deliverables to Acme: POC playbook (attached), capacity profile (attached), and a quote for reserved pool + burst usage.

Commercial note: we can offer a pilot discount on reserved pool (10% off the first month) and expedite procurement paperwork if they want to move to a paid pilot. Laura, suggest we prepare a short commercial summary to send to procurement and include the reserved capacity addendum and a sample SOW.

— Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity vs Hyperscaler GPU eval — recap + proposed next tests

Jordan / Procurement — thanks for the questions. TL;DR: yes, we can provide a written addendum for reserved capacity (SLA + latency SLO), we support a configurable burst buffer (we recommend enabling a 2.5x burst for your POC), and failover is automatic with warm standby (expected cutover ~90–180s — we’ll measure).

Commercial / next steps: 
- Attached: redwood_quote_v1.pdf (POC quote), redwood_poc-plan.pdf, redwood_capacity_profile.xlsx.
- Pilot pricing: for the suggested 4x 80GB-class GPU reserved pool we’ve priced a 14-day POC at an equivalent pro-rated monthly rate of $XX,XXX (see quote). We can apply a 10% pilot discount for Acme.
- Legal/commercial: I’ve included links to the Master Services Agreement + Reserved Capacity addendum for signature: https://www.docusign.com/exec/ABC123456789. If Procurement confirms, we can get the addendum signed and provision the pool within 3 business days of execution.

POC dates: we propose Mar 10–13 for kickoff + configuration and run test starting Mar 13–16. Please confirm:
- Which model(s) will you test (open weights, custom finetune, etc.)?
- Who from Acme will be the technical lead for the kickoff (name/email)?
- Procurement: please confirm PO/approval path or if you prefer an initial SOW instead.

We’ll hold the proposed window pending your confirmation. If helpful, we can set a 30-minute kickoff call next week — suggest Mar 5–6.

Thanks — excited to get this moving.

— Markus Klein
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
